note: Independent source rejudgment against complete RFC 9552 Section 5.2.3.1: ‘The OSPF Route Type TLV MUST be included in the advertisement when the type is either being signaled explicitly in the underlying LSA or can be determined via another LSA for the same prefix when it is not signaled explicitly (e.g., in the case of OSPFv2 Extended Prefix Opaque LSA [RFC7684]).’ Read both tagged tests and their producers. internal/plugins/ospf/rfc9552_bgpls_export_route_type_test.go::TestRFC9552ExtendedPrefixResolvesRouteType installs actual Router, Summary Network, AS External and NSSA LSAs plus an Extended Prefix LSA, then synchronously requests the live publisher snapshot. Ten cases assert exactly one opaque-marked extended advertisement for router 2.2.2.2 and the exact route type: underlying zero resolves to each of 1 through 6; explicit AS/NSSA classes each distinguish Type 1 from Type 2. The opaque provenance guard prevents a base prefix alone satisfying the test; NSSA in another area exercises the cross-bucket lookup. internal/plugins/ospf/bgpls_export.go::publishBGPLSLocked processes base LSAs before extensions; v2 dispatches Extended Prefix LSAs to extendedV2Prefix, which consumes v2PrefixRouteTypes results and publishes RouteType on the prefix. The exporter subscription in internal/component/bgp/plugins/ls_export/export_plugin.go forwards source snapshots to replace; export_state.go::replace calls encodeTopology, and reconcile forwards encoded routes. export_encode.go::encodeTopology copies RouteType into PrefixDescriptor.OSPFRouteType, whose encoder emits nonzero values as TLV 264. internal/component/bgp/plugins/ls_export/export_rfc9552_polarity_test.go::TestRFC9552NativeOSPFRouteType independently drives replacement/reconciliation and asserts exactly TLV 264 value 1 in the captured prefix NLRI. This composes two unit boundaries; the LSDB test does not itself inspect BGP wire bytes, and the exporter test does not exercise all six route types or a live BGP peer. The single-positive annotation is valid for this origination obligation, not an exemption for underlying zero or a receive-refusal assertion. The owned edit is an ordinary exhaustive comment in the fixture switch, outside the tag claim; it requires audit rejudgment but does not by itself change discrimination behavior or claim hashes. Stored producer-halt records were read, not replayed or independently freshness-verified. Concurrent producer changes are not attributed to this comment edit.
